thread:
Maya (CS): Weekly BrightPath health check — can we get p95 / p99 by route + model and streaming vs non-streaming for the last 7 days? Call out any anomalies. We have a renewal check on Friday, want to surface risks.

Raj (SE): On it. Pulling metrics now, pinging @Linus for runtime validation.

Linus (Eng Runtime): putting the short table here, numbers are 7d rolling, us-east region (avg traffic for BP).
```
Route | Model | Streaming | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | note
generate.text | redwood-v2-13b | non-streaming | 420 ms | 980 ms | elevated p99 on Mon 09:12 UTC
generate.text | redwood-v2-13b | streaming | 510 ms | 1,280 ms | KV cache cold + autoscaler microburst
chat.complete | gpt-open-7b | non-streaming | 180 ms | 420 ms | stable
chat.complete | gpt-open-7b | streaming | 210 ms | 560 ms | small tail
embeddings.create | emb-sim-1 | non-streaming | 85 ms | 150 ms | normal
```

Linus (Eng Runtime): Quick notes — the biggest pain is streaming p99 on redwood-v2-13b. We saw a 3-minute window Monday where requests hit nodes after a scale event, KV cache missed, and latency tail spiked. Autoscaler cooldown kept cold workers in rotation for ~90s which magnified p99.

Maya (CS): Oof, ok. How much did that impact BrightPath's spend/SLAs?

Linus (Eng Runtime): Rough estimate: that spike added ~12% extra billed token time for that customer window (retries and longer token times). Overall weekly spend bump ~+4% vs baseline because of a couple of prolonged requests.

Olivia (CSM): Flagging renewal risk as "moderate" if we don't reduce p99 >1s on their generate route. They called out realtime UX being sensitive. Recommend an enablement session to tweak prompts + routing.

Raj (SE): Agreed. Short-term mitigations we can roll today: enable prefix KV warming for their prefix, reduce max batch timeout on their route, and set a canary to route traffic to a Dedicated pool during peak hours. I'll open the canary and post config.

Raj (SE): Config snippet for canary / batching (will apply to BrightPath route):
```json
{"route":"generate.text","model":"redwood-v2-13b","batching":{"max_batch_tokens":2048,"timeout_ms":8},"kv_cache":"prefix"}
```

Linus (Eng Runtime): That config looks good. Also recommend temporary throttling of very large max_tokens per request (e.g., cap at 1024) and enabling aggressive KV pre-warming for their top prefixes for the next 48h.

Maya (CS): Can we commit to a remediation timeline before Friday?

Raj (SE): I'll push the canary today and monitor. Expect initial effects within 30–60m after warm. Will report numbers here.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: applied pool adjustments for customer BrightPath (bp-42) at 1753002900.

Linus (Eng Runtime): After canary + pre-warm: quick re-check numbers for the rolling 1h window post-change — p95/p99 improved:
```
generate.text | redwood-v2-13b | non-streaming | 380 ms | 720 ms
generate.text | redwood-v2-13b | streaming | 430 ms | 820 ms
```

Olivia (CSM): Nice improvement. I'll book the enablement session Wed 10am PT with their eng. We'll also include a short cost/behavior primer.

Maya (CS): Thanks everyone. Action items: Raj — canary + config (today). Linus — KV pre-warm and monitor p99 (today). Olivia — enablement invite + renewal messaging (Tue). We'll reconvene here Thurs for a final pre-renewal status. :thumbsup:

Raj (SE): Will post a follow-up metric dump with exact graphs and the per-route CSV later today. :white_check_mark:

Linus (Eng Runtime): FYI, long-term reduce tail by adding sticky routing for high-QPS clients to dedicated pools and improving autoscaler cooldown heuristics. Filed ENG-RUNTIME-924.

Maya (CS): Copy that. Thanks team.
